headline: Suspected ShinyHunters leader arrested in Netherlands, accused of planning two murders
summary: The 24-year-old man is linked to high-profile attacks on the FBI, Rockstar Games, and Ticketmaster, and is also suspected of attempted incitement to commit two murders.
details: Dutch police have arrested a 24-year-old man in Amsterdam, identified by reports as Pepijn van der Stap, on September 15th. He is linked to the ShinyHunters hacking group, known for claiming responsibility for breaches at Ticketmaster, Rockstar Games, and the FBI.

While Dutch authorities and the FBI have not officially named the suspect, reports from Krebs on Security and Reuters identified him. Van der Stap was previously convicted for data theft and extortion in 2023, though ShinyHunters denies any association with him.

Brett Leatherman, assistant director of the FBI’s Cyber Division, called the suspect one of the group’s alleged leaders. He issued a warning to remaining members, stating, "The longer you stay in this, the more we learn about you."

Adding to the charges, the 24-year-old is also suspected of "attempted incitement to commit two murders," according to Dutch police. FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed ongoing investigations with partners based on this arrest.

topic: tesla secures 30b credit lines for cybercab optimus
headline_marked: [[Tesla secures $30B in new credit lines]] to scale Cybercab, Optimus, and Semi production
headline: Tesla secures $30B in new credit lines to scale Cybercab, Optimus, and Semi production
summary: Tesla has secured $30 billion in new credit facilities from Citibank and Wells Fargo, earmarked for scaling production of its upcoming Cybercab robotaxi, Optimus robot, and Semi truck.
details: Tesla has secured $30 billion in fresh credit lines to help scale its new products: the Cybercab robotaxi, Optimus robot, and Tesla Semi. This significant financing will support the company's ambitious manufacturing plans for these ventures.

The funding includes a $20 billion three-year delayed-draw term loan facility from Citibank and an $8 billion five-year revolving credit facility from Wells Fargo. An additional $2 billion revolving credit facility with a 364-day term was also signed with Wells Fargo.

Despite securing these funds, Tesla stated in a regulatory filing that it does not intend to draw on these loan facilities this year. The company has already projected capital expenditures of at least $25 billion for 2026.

Tesla ended the second quarter of this year with approximately $9 billion in debt, alongside a substantial cash and investments pile exceeding $40 billion. The new credit lines provide a strong financial buffer for future expansion.

All three products—Cybercab, Optimus, and Semi—require new manufacturing lines. Tesla is adopting a strategy of building dedicated new factories for the Semi and Optimus robot to facilitate their production.
